analysis.objective: Swap src/components/CodeEditor.tsx from the hand-rolled regex-highlighted <textarea>/<pre> overlay to a CodeMirror 6-based editor that provides working JS/TS autocomplete, automatic bracket/quote closing, and correct cursor placement while preserving the existing zustand store contract.
analysis.successDefinition: CodeEditor.tsx mounts a CodeMirror 6 EditorView (no <textarea>/<pre> overlay, no Monaco code path) built from @codemirror/view, @codemirror/state, @codemirror/lang-javascript (javascript() + typescript()), @codemirror/autocomplete, and @codemirror/commands. Typing {, (, [, or " inserts the closing partner and leaves the caret between them; typing the closing char over the auto-inserted partner does not duplicate it. The caret and selection remain exactly where expected after plain typing, bracket auto-close, and selection replacement, and setCursorPos reports the correct line/column. Autocomplete triggers and inserts completions in both JS and TS. Every edit persists via saveCode, and switching lang or problem loads the correct state[lang]/starter value with no update loop. npm run build (tsc -b && vite build) and npm run lint pass; the editor uses no web workers and only tree-shakeable per-package @codemirror dependencies (no monaco bundle).
assumptions: CodeMirror 6 packages (@codemirror/view, @codemirror/state, @codemirror/lang-javascript, @codemirror/autocomplete, @codemirror/commands) will be installed via npm with registry access available; none are in package.json today.

The zustand store contract is fixed and out of scope to change: CodeEditor remains a self-contained default-export component, driven by lang ('js'|'ts'), value from state[lang] || problem.starter[lang], and writing back via saveCode(code) and setCursorPos(line, col).
Both languages share one editor instance; switching lang swaps the language extension and document rather than mounting a second editor.
Existing editor behaviors not part of the four complaints (Tab indentation, Enter indent continuation, Cmd/Ctrl+/ comment toggle) must be preserved in the swap to avoid regressions.
The regex highlighter, .tk-* classes, and the <pre> overlay are removed along with the textarea; the existing .editor-pane/.editor-body layout from EditorPane remains and CodeMirror must fit it.
Autocomplete scope is package-provided syntax/identifier completion from @codemirror/lang-javascript and @codemirror/autocomplete; no language server or harness-aware completion is implied.
On a bad/empty input (no starter code, missing state[lang]) the editor renders an empty document rather than crashing; this is handled by the existing getProblemState fallback.
risks: Store/editor update loop: CodeMirror's onUpdate -> saveCode -> store value -> editor update can ping-pong; an external-vs-internal change guard is required.
CodeMirror's default CSS can clash with the existing .editor-pane/gutter layout, breaking line numbers, scroll sync, or overlay alignment; a matching theme/measure may be needed.
Quote auto-closing via closebrackets is context-sensitive and can misbehave (e.g. auto-closing inside an existing string); must be verified against the JS language context rules.
Autocomplete may fail to trigger for TS unless typescript() language configuration and completion source are wired correctly; needs explicit verification for both lang values.
tsc strict + React 19 type-checking against CodeMirror 6 generics (Transaction, StateEffect, ViewUpdate) can surface type errors that block npm run build.
If install/build fails partway, regressing to the hand-rolled editor or Monaco would contradict the caller's explicit CodeMirror 6 choice and leave the four issues unfixed.
outOfScope: Removing @monaco-editor/react/monaco from package.json — the acceptance criteria do not require dependency cleanup, only that Monaco is not used.
Real-time TypeScript diagnostics/lint in the gutter — would require an LSP or web-worker compiler, violating the client-side-only, no-web-worker constraint.
Editor theming, font/preference settings, vim/emacs keymaps, and find/replace panels — beyond the four stated criteria.
Refactoring the zustand store or its consumers of cursorLine/cursorCol — the editor must fit the existing contract, not change it.
Rebuilding autocomplete from the problem's harness/solution signature — completion is syntax/identifier-based from the language package, not harness-aware.
Touch-ups to other inputs (test-case editors, filter/search fields) — only src/components/CodeEditor.tsx is in scope.

discoveryFindings.finding: src/components/CodeEditor.tsx is a hand-rolled regex-highlighted <textarea> overlaid on a <pre> (#hl) with a separate gutter (.nums div), using one giant HL_RE with 10 capture groups mapped to .tk-* classes. It takes NO props — it is a self-contained component (both named `export function CodeEditor` and `export default CodeEditor`) that reads `lang`, `currentSlug`, `getProblem`, `getProblemState`, `saveCode`, `setCursorPos` straight from the zustand store, and derives `value = state[lang] || problem?.starter[lang] || ""` in the render body.
discoveryFindings.implication: The CodeMirror 6 swap keeps the same zero-prop contract: the new component must continue self-reading the store. Remove HL_RE/HL_CLS/esc/highlight/renderNums and the .tk-* classes together with the <textarea>/<pre>/gutter markup.

discoveryFindings.finding: Contrary to the roadmap's stale 'missing-editor-keyboard-handling' finding, the current CodeEditor ALREADY implements Tab (2-space indent / shift-tab dedent / multi-line block indent), Enter auto-indent continuation (copies leading whitespace, +2 spaces after /[{([:]\s*$/), and Cmd/Ctrl+/ comment toggle, all inside one onKeyDown handler; saveCode is called on every onInput.
discoveryFindings.implication: The task's assumption #4 ('Tab indentation, Enter indent continuation, Cmd/Ctrl+/ comment toggle must be preserved') is grounded in real existing behavior, not just the prototype. CodeMirror must reproduce these (indentWithTab/keymap, autocompletion-friendly Enter, toggleComment) or they are a regression.

discoveryFindings.finding: Caret tracking is via onSelect/onKeyUp/onClick -> trackCaret(), which computes 1-based `line` (split by \n) and 1-based `col` (selectionStart - lastIndexOf("\n"), i.e. the first column is 1) and calls setCursorPos(line, col).
discoveryFindings.implication: CodeMirror's posToLineColumn is 1-based line but 0-based column; the swap must add 1 to the column (or use posToLineColumn().to + 1) so StatusBar's 'Ln X, Col Y' and the store's cursorLine/cursorCol keep matching semantics, and setCursorPos must fire on CodeMirror selection updates.

discoveryFindings.finding: Store confirms the contract: `lang: 'js' | 'ts'`; per-problem state `{ js: string | null, ts: string | null, ... }`; `saveCode(code)` writes to problems[currentSlug][lang]; `setCursorPos(line, col)` sets `cursorLine`/`cursorCol` (defaults 1/1); `getProblemState(slug)` lazily mutates the store (set on first access, so safe in render but re-renders on any store change). Store is persisted to localStorage key `leetlab.v2` via partialize (lang, split, lastSlug, problems).
discoveryFindings.implication: No store changes needed — the plan's 'store contract is fixed and out of scope' assumption holds. But because getProblemState re-renders on every store write, the CodeMirror onUpdate->saveCode path must guard against feeding the saved value back into the EditorView (external-vs-internal change guard), or it will ping-pong.

discoveryFindings.finding: EditorPane mounts `<CodeEditor />` with zero props (line 211), sandwiched between `.editor-head` (JS/TS seg buttons that call `useAppStore.getState().setLang`) and `.editor-foot` (Run/Submit buttons). handleRun independently reads `st[lang] || prob.starter[lang]` from the store and runs via tsCompiler.compile for ts — so the store, not the editor DOM, is the run source of truth.
discoveryFindings.implication: The swap is isolated to CodeEditor.tsx: EditorPane needs no edits. The editor must keep persisting to saveCode on every doc change so Run/Submit see current code, and switching lang (setLang) must trigger the document/language swap inside CodeEditor (shared single EditorView is fine).

The 13px/1.62/var(--mono) metrics and 14px padding should be carried into the CodeMirror theme so it visually matches; CodeMirror's default CSS (baseTheme) will otherwise clash with the fixed 52px gutter and overlay alignment.

Two `new EditorView` calls, or a view recreated on every render
No destroy in cleanup, leaving an EditorView attached to detached DOM

rubric.label: StrictMode double-mount is idempotent

rubric.ruleStatement: Exactly one EditorView exists per component mount; switching JS↔TS reconfigures that same view in place and never re-creates the view or its DOM node.
passCriteria: The CodeEditor mounts the EditorView exactly once (single guarded init in an effect/ref) and the DOM node the view is attached to keeps its identity across a JS→TS toggle.
A lang change applies the new language via `view.dispatch({ effects: StateEffect.reconfigure.of(...) })`; no `new EditorView` call exists on the lang-change path.
Undo history, scroll position, and the live selection survive a JS→TS→JS round-trip with the document text unchanged.
No `key={lang}`-style remount of the editor container exists anywhere in the component tree.
failureExamples: Toggling TS→JS visibly re-initializes the editor: cursor jumps to top, scroll resets, undo history is emptied.
The component creates a fresh EditorView on every lang change, leaking the previous view instance.
Two EditorView instances (one per language) are swapped by mounting/unmounting instead of reconfiguring one.

rubric.label: Syntax highlighting follows the store lang
rubric.ruleStatement: The active language extension in the view always matches the zustand `lang` value, so tokenization is correct per language and the swap is driven by the store `setLang` (the JS/TS seg buttons), never by editor-internal state.
passCriteria: With `lang=ts`, a document containing TS-only syntax (interface, generics, type annotations) renders those tokens with highlight styles; switching to `js` re-renders the same document with JS-only tokenization.
Clicking the JS/TS seg button (which calls `setLang`) flips both the store `lang` and the editor's active language in the same frame, with no extra click or reload.
`view.state.facet(language)` resolves to `typescript()` when store lang is 'ts' and `javascript()` when it is 'js'.
The document text is never mutated by the swap — no whitespace/indent/token rewrite from the highlight layer.
failureExamples: A TS document shows no highlighting for `interface`/generic tokens because only `javascript()` was wired for both languages.
The editor keeps tokenizing as JS after the seg button already shows TypeScript active.
Swapping languages reformats or rewrites the user's source text.

rubric.label: Autocomplete for the language being edited
rubric.ruleStatement: Per the caller acceptance criterion — 'Editor provides autocomplete for the language being edited (JS and TS)' — working autocomplete must exist in both languages, sourced from the active lang extension rather than one hardwired JS completion source.
passCriteria: With lang='js', typing `console.` opens a completion popup listing console members (log, error, warn); selecting one inserts it correctly.
With lang='ts', completions include TS-specific symbols (declared types/interfaces/type keywords) and are not limited to the JS global set.
The completion source is composed from the active `javascript()`/`typescript()` extension; no hand-rolled or JS-only completion source overrides it in either language.
Accepting a completion (Tab/Enter) replaces exactly the intended prefix and the cursor lands at the correct position.
failureExamples: No completion popup appears when typing `.` after an identifier in either language.
TS mode offers only the JS global completion set because a single javascript()-based autocomplete is registered for both languages.
Completions from the wrong language appear — e.g., JS keywords offered while editing a TS document.

rubric.label: Repeated toggling is idempotent and leak-free
rubric.ruleStatement: Toggling JS↔TS any number of times reaches the same state as a single toggle: no duplicate language extensions or completion sources accumulate, and the editor remains fully functional afterwards.
passCriteria: After 10 rapid JS→TS→JS→TS toggles, `view.state.facet(language)` holds exactly one language value and behavior matches a fresh single toggle.
Rapid toggling never throws, blanks the document, or leaves the view broken (dead completions, frozen typing).
Undo history survives toggles: Ctrl+Z after a toggle still undoes the last text edit, not the language switch.
No more than one language facet / completion source is present in the reconfigured state after any number of toggles.
failureExamples: After several toggles, typing no longer completes or the popup shows duplicated entries.
The editor throws on the third toggle because extensions were appended to the configuration instead of replaced.
The language switch itself lands in the undo stack, so Ctrl+Z after a toggle undoes the language change instead of the edit.

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure is an append-not-replace or remount pattern — the lang-change path either builds up duplicate language facets/extensions on every toggle or tears down and recreates the EditorView, so reset the store of extensions to a freshly built array (language + autocomplete) each time and apply it with a single `view.dispatch({ effects: StateEffect.reconfigure.of([...]) })` on the one view you mounted once.

phases.name: Wire the zustand store contract: saveCode, setCursorPos, doc sync with update-loop guard
phases.goal: Complete the store contract bridge: dispatch saveCode(doc) on user document changes; on lang/problem switch dispatch replaceDocument with state[lang] || starter[lang]; on selection updates call setCursorPos with 1-based line and (CodeMirror's 0-based column + 1) to match the old semantics; and guard external-vs-internal changes so the onUpdate -> saveCode -> store re-render (getProblemState re-renders on every write) path does not ping-pong.
phases.expectedResult: Every edit persists to problems[currentSlug][lang] via saveCode with no update loop; switching lang loads the correct state[lang]/starter document and swaps the language extension; StatusBar 'Ln X, Col Y' and store cursorLine/cursorCol match the hand-rolled 1-based semantics (line 1-based, column 1-based).

rubric.label: Every user edit persists to the store
rubric.ruleStatement: Each user-originated document change in the editor must result in problems[currentSlug][lang] holding exactly the editor's current doc content via saveCode — inspect the zustand store after edits, not the plan text.
passCriteria: Typing characters, deleting, and pasting each leaves store problems[currentSlug][lang] === EditorView doc.toString() at every read after the change
Triggering an autocomplete accept followed by typing persists the completed text, not the pre-completion fragment
After a rapid burst of keystrokes (e.g. 20 chars) the store's final value equals the final doc with no partial/earlier snapshots surviving
Switching to a different problem and back reloads the previously persisted value, proving the write survived in the store, not just in the editor
failureExamples: Store value stays at the starter document while the editor shows typed text
Only the first keystroke is persisted and subsequent edits are dropped
Store contains stale/duplicated content (doc + prefix) after paste or completion
Returning to a problem shows blank or starter code despite prior edits

rubric.label: External-vs-internal change guard prevents the update loop
rubric.ruleStatement: The onUpdate -> saveCode -> store re-render (getProblemState re-renders on every write) path must not feed back into saveCode; programmatic dispatch of state[lang]/starter must be distinguishable from user edits and must not re-trigger writes — verify by observing store write counts, not by re-reading the guard code.
passCriteria: With the editor idle (no user input), the number of saveCode dispatches stays constant over a 3-second observation window
Loading a doc via lang/problem switch triggers exactly one store write (or zero if the loaded value already equals state[lang]) and never an infinite render cycle
The tab does not thrash/hang and the React render counter stabilizes after every user edit
Manually calling getProblemState/setState to reload the same value does not cause a new saveCode dispatch
failureExamples: Console/React DevTools shows an ever-growing dispatch or render count while the editor is untouched
After one keystroke the store write count increments continuously (infinite ping-pong), eventually freezing the UI
Switching langs triggers a cascade of writes that resets the doc or resets cursor to 0:0
The store write count doubles per edit, indicating write-feedback

rubric.label: Lang/problem switch loads the right document
rubric.ruleStatement: On lang or problem switch the editor must replaceDocument with state[lang] when present, else starter[lang], and must not clobber a language's saved doc with another language's content or with starter — verify by switching and inspecting both the editor and the store after each switch.
passCriteria: Switching JS->TS->JS returns the exact JS doc that existed before, including any unsaved-in-editor-but-saved-in-store edits
A language never touched by the user loads its starter[lang] content
Switching problems while edits exist in the current lang does not overwrite problems[otherSlug][lang]
The language extension (javascript()/typescript()) swaps with the doc so the loaded content is highlighted/completed per the active lang
failureExamples: Switching to TS shows the JS doc content in a TS-highlighted view
Returning to a language shows starter text, erasing prior persisted edits
The doc shows the previous problem's code after switching problems
Language extension lags one switch behind the loaded doc

rubric.label: Cursor stays correctly placed after typing, bracket auto-close, and selection replacement — no misplacement bugs remain
rubric.ruleStatement: The caller's acceptance criterion: Cursor stays correctly placed after typing, bracket auto-close, and selection replacement — no misplacement bugs remain. Verify by typing, auto-closing, and replacing selections and reading EditorView state.selection.main each time.
passCriteria: Typing a character positions the caret exactly after the inserted char (never before it, never at 0:0)
Typing '(' or '[' or '{' or a quote leaves the caret between the opener and the auto-inserted closer, and typing the closer advances past it without duplicating it
Selecting a range and typing replaces exactly the selection with the caret immediately after the replacement text
Undo/redo after bracket close and selection replacement restores both content and a sane caret position
failureExamples: After typing '(' the caret sits after the closing ')'
After replacing a selection the caret jumps to doc start or to the end of the line
Auto-close of a quote leaves the caret outside the pair or inserts an extra closer
Caret lands at column 0 or line 0 after ordinary typing

rubric.label: setCursorPos matches hand-rolled 1-based semantics
rubric.ruleStatement: On every selection update the editor must call setCursorPos(1-based line, 0-based column + 1) so store cursorLine/cursorCol agree with the StatusBar 'Ln X, Col Y' display and with the old textarea semantics — verify by reading the store and StatusBar after moving the caret, not by tracing call sites.
passCriteria: Placing the caret on visual line 2, first column sets store cursorLine=2, cursorCol=1 and StatusBar reads 'Ln 2, Col 1'
At the end of a 30-char line store cursorCol equals 31 and StatusBar reads 'Col 31'
Clicking, arrow-keying, and selection-anchoring all update the store values immediately with no stale lag
cursorLine/cursorCol never report 0 for a valid caret position
failureExamples: StatusBar shows 'Ln 2, Col 0' or store cursorCol is 0-based
After clicking mid-line the store reports the previous caret position
StatusBar and store disagree with each other after a selection
After bracket auto-close the reported column is off by one from the actual caret

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure: onUpdate fires for programmatic replaceDocument/reconfiguration too, so the store re-render re-dispatches saveCode and the component ping-pongs (or cursor jumps to 0:0) — fastest fix is to no-op the saveCode dispatch when the incoming doc equals the last value written to the store (and skip setCursorPos for non-user transactions), which also resolves the off-by-one cursor complaints.

phases.name: Preserve Tab/Enter/Cmd+Ctrl+// keybindings
phases.goal: Reproduce the existing keyboard behaviors CodeMirror must not regress (discovery confirms they exist today in the onKeyDown handler): Tab = 2-space indent / Shift-Tab = dedent including multi-line block indent, Enter = newline + indent continuation, Cmd/Ctrl+/ = toggleComment, plus defaultKeymap/historyKeymap for undo/redo/selectAll, via indentWithTab and a composed keymap.
inputs: existing onKeyDown behavior in current CodeEditor.tsx (indent, indent continuation, comment toggle)
phases.expectedResult: Tab, Shift-Tab, Enter (newline + indent continuation), and Cmd/Ctrl+/ toggleComment behave exactly as in the hand-rolled editor; undo/redo/select-all work; no keyboard regressions.

rubric.label: Tab indent / Shift-Tab dedent parity
rubric.ruleStatement: Tab inserts a 2-space indent at the caret, Shift-Tab dedents by 2 spaces, and with a multi-line selection both apply to every selected line exactly as the hand-rolled onKeyDown handler did.
passCriteria: Tab at a caret on a line with no selection inserts exactly two space characters (never a literal \t or focus loss)
Shift-Tab on an already-unindented line is a no-op and does not move focus or delete content
With a selection spanning 3+ lines, Shift-Tab removes exactly 2 leading spaces from every selected line
With a selection spanning 3+ lines, Tab adds exactly 2 leading spaces to every selected line while preserving relative indentation between lines
failureExamples: Tab inserts a literal tab character or moves focus out of the editor
Shift-Tab on a multi-line selection dedents only the first line
Tab on an empty line at depth 4 produces 6 or 8 spaces instead of 4 (depth mismatch)

rubric.label: Enter newline + indent continuation
rubric.ruleStatement: Enter produces a newline that carries forward the preceding line's indentation, matching the hand-rolled continuation behavior.
passCriteria: Enter on a line indented N spaces produces a new line with the caret at exactly N spaces
Enter mid-line splits the line and applies the source line's leading indentation to the new line
Five consecutive Enter presses keep all resulting lines at the same indentation level with no drift
failureExamples: Enter resets the caret to column 0 of the new line
Enter double-indents the new line to N+2 or more spaces
Enter on a line with trailing code carries trailing whitespace or inserts extra blank lines

rubric.label: Cmd/Ctrl+/ comment toggle
rubric.ruleStatement: Cmd/Ctrl+/ toggles a // line comment on the current line or on every line of a multi-line selection, and pressing it again reverses the change.
passCriteria: Cmd+/ on an uncommented line prefixes it with // at the line's indentation depth
Cmd+/ on an already-commented line removes exactly the // prefix
Cmd+/ on a selection spanning multiple lines toggles the comment on every selected line, not just the first
The browser default find/search binding is not triggered; the editor consumes the Cmd+/ event
failureExamples: Cmd+/ opens the browser find dialog or inserts a literal '/' character into the document
Toggling a multi-line selection comments only the first line
The toggle writes // at column 0 instead of at the line's indentation

rubric.label: Composed keymap with undo/redo/select-all intact
rubric.ruleStatement: The custom bindings are composed as CodeMirror extension keymaps (indentWithTab, toggleComment, defaultKeymap, historyKeymap) with custom bindings ordered before the defaults so nothing is shadowed, and no DOM-level onKeyDown interception remains.
passCriteria: Cmd+Z undoes the last edit and Cmd+Shift+Z redoes it after custom bindings have fired
Cmd+A selects the full document
All four custom bindings (Tab, Shift-Tab, Enter, Cmd+/) still fire while defaultKeymap/historyKeymap are present in the same keymap array
Inspection of the deliverable shows keybindings registered via the CodeMirror keymap extension mechanism and no onKeyDown handler on the editor DOM element
failureExamples: Cmd+Z silently stops working after a custom binding fires because a custom keymap shadows historyKeymap
The deliverable still contains a hand-rolled onKeyDown DOM handler intercepting keys outside CodeMirror's keymap mechanism
Cmd+A no longer works after adding a custom binding to the keymap array

rubric.label: Repeatable, drift-free key sequences
rubric.ruleStatement: Every preserved keybinding is repeatable and reversible: applying the same key sequence twice yields the doubled expected result or returns the document to its exact baseline, so behavior does not drift on repeated use.
passCriteria: Tab pressed twice produces +4 spaces and Shift-Tab pressed twice restores the original column
Cmd+/ pressed twice returns the document to its byte-for-byte pre-toggle content
Repeated Enter presses keep every generated line at the same indentation (no per-press drift)
failureExamples: Tab indentation accumulates incorrectly on the third consecutive press
Comment toggle is asymmetric (two presses to start, one to uncomment)
Enter indentation drifts by one space per line over several presses

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure is the composed keymap being wrong — Tab moves focus because indentWithTab was left out, or Cmd+/ is swallowed by defaultKeymap — so the fastest fix is to set the keymap array to [indentWithTab, toggleComment, defaultKeymap, historyKeymap] (custom bindings first) and rerun the four parity keystrokes against the old editor.

phases.name: Add closebrackets bracket/quote auto-close
phases.goal: Add closeBrackets() and closeBracketsKeymap so typing {, (, [, or " auto-inserts the closing partner and leaves the caret between them; typing the closing char over the auto-inserted partner does not duplicate it, respecting JS/TS language context (no auto-close inside an existing string literal).
phases.expectedResult: Auto-insertion of (), [], {}, and "" with the caret between opening and closing char; no duplicated closing char when typed over the partner; string-context safety verified for both js and ts.

rubric.label: Opening chars insert closing partners with caret between
rubric.ruleStatement: Typing an opening { ( or [ or " auto-inserts the closing partner and leaves the cursor between them.
passCriteria: Typing { at a code position produces {} with the caret between the two characters.
Typing ( produces (), typing [ produces [], and typing " produces "" with the caret between.
Exactly one closing character is inserted per keystroke: repeating the same opening char N times yields exactly N pairs with no stacking (repeatability/idempotency).
The behavior holds in both the js and ts buffers.
failureExamples: Typing { inserts only { with no partner.
The caret lands after the closing partner instead of between the pair.
Typing " inserts "" but the caret sits after both quotes.

rubric.label: Typing the closing char over the partner does not duplicate
rubric.ruleStatement: Typing the closing char over the auto-inserted partner does not duplicate it: when the caret sits immediately before a matching closing character, the keystroke moves the caret past it without inserting a second copy.
passCriteria: After { auto-closes to {}, typing } moves the caret past the existing } without changing the text.
The skip-over behavior holds for ), ], and " as well.
Typing a closer N consecutive times leaves exactly one closing character in the document.
failureExamples: Typing } after {} produces }}.
Typing " after "" produces """ and traps the caret between the duplicates.

rubric.label: No auto-close inside strings or comments
rubric.ruleStatement: Auto-close respects JS/TS lexical context: no partner is inserted when the caret is inside a string literal or comment. This is the correctness invariant that separates the language-aware closeBrackets from a naive keydown reimplementation, and it must hold for both js and ts.
passCriteria: Typing {, (, [, or " inside an existing single-quoted, double-quoted, or template string inserts nothing.
Typing " immediately after a word character (e.g. don followed by ") does not auto-close.
Auto-close fires nothing inside // or /* */ comments.
Verified with both the js and ts language configured.
failureExamples: Typing { inside const s = "a{b"; produces "a{b}".
Auto-close fires inside a comment, mangling the commented text.

rubric.label: Store value and cursor pos stay in sync with the buffer
rubric.ruleStatement: Every auto-close transaction propagates to the zustand store so state[lang] matches the editor buffer for the current lang, and setCursorPos reports the caret at the post-edit position.
passCriteria: After an auto-close keystroke, the store's state[lang] value contains the closing partner visible in the editor.
setCursorPos fires after the edit and reports the caret line/col between the pair.
Switching lang away and back, or reloading persisted state, keeps the auto-closed text intact.
failureExamples: The editor displays {} but the store still holds the pre-keystroke text, so the closing bracket vanishes on lang switch or reload.
cursorLine/cursorCol in the store lag one keystroke behind the visible caret.

rubric.label: Deleting a bracket removes its auto-inserted partner
rubric.ruleStatement: Deleting one side of an auto-inserted pair removes the partner too, so the document is never left with a dangling closing char and the compensated deletion reaches the store (rollback safety for the destructive Backspace/Delete actions).
passCriteria: Backspacing over the opening { of {} removes both characters in one action.
Delete (forward) at the closing partner removes the whole pair.
The store value after pair deletion matches the editor buffer.
failureExamples: Backspacing { in {} leaves a stray } in the document and in the store.
Delete leaves an orphaned opening {.

phases.healerHint: Most likely fail: Backspace/Delete leaves a dangling closing char because closeBracketsKeymap was never composed into the EditorView's keymap extensions — add keymap.of(closeBracketsKeymap) next to closeBrackets() and re-run the pair-deletion checks.

phases.name: Enable JS/TS identifier autocomplete
phases.goal: Add autocompletion() with activation on typing plus the javascript()/typescript() completion source so identifier/keyword completions trigger and insert in both js and ts documents, with Enter accepting a completion while the popup is open and plain Enter still producing newline+indent otherwise.
phases.expectedResult: Autocomplete popup triggers on typing and inserts completions correctly in both js and ts; Enter accepts the active completion; no LSP or web-worker involvement.

rubric.label: JS/TS completion matches the active language
rubric.ruleStatement: The editor provides autocomplete for the language being edited (JS and TS) — the caller's acceptance criterion, verbatim — meaning the completion source is the @codemirror/lang-javascript javascript()/typescript() source matched to the store's active lang, not a static shared list.
passCriteria: In a JS document, typing an identifier prefix (e.g. 'fun', 'ret') opens a popup listing JS completions (function, return, const, ...).
In a TS document, the popup includes TS-specific completions (interface, type, enum, readonly, as, keyof, ...).
The completion list is tied to the active document language: switching lang js↔ts changes which completions appear, with no page reload.
Repeatedly switching js↔ts never doubles the popup or lists the same completion twice.
failureExamples: The same hardcoded completion list appears in both js and ts documents.
A TS document only ever offers JS completions, with no type/interface/keywords.
Completions work in exactly one language; the other shows no popup at all.
Each lang switch adds a second popup or duplicated completion entries.

rubric.label: Completion insertion is clean and repeatable
rubric.ruleStatement: Accepting a completion replaces only the typed prefix and inserts the chosen text without duplicating, dropping, or mangling adjacent characters, and repeated accept/undo cycles leave the document byte-identical to the initial state.
passCriteria: Typing 'fu' then accepting 'function' yields exactly 'function' in the document — no leftover 'fu', no doubled characters.
After insertion the caret sits at the end of the inserted completion and the next typed character lands there.
Accepting a completion while a range is selected replaces the selection rather than appending after it.
Accept → undo → accept again restores byte-identical content with no accumulated corruption.
failureExamples: Accepting 'function' from prefix 'fu' leaves 'fufunction' or 'functionfu' in the document.
Inserted completion drops or overwrites the character just after the caret.
Undo/redo after a completion corrupts the buffer, deletes lines, or duplicates text.

rubric.label: Enter accepts completions or newlines, contextually
rubric.ruleStatement: Enter accepts the active completion while the popup is open, but produces newline plus indentation when the popup is closed — the completion keymap must not shadow the default newline behavior, and vice versa.
passCriteria: With a completion popup open, pressing Enter inserts the highlighted completion and closes the popup.
With the popup closed, pressing Enter inserts a newline, carries forward the current indentation, and adds a level after an open '{' (matching pre-swap behavior).
Pressing Enter while the popup is open but nothing is selected neither eats the newline nor inserts junk.
failureExamples: Enter always inserts a newline, so the popup can never be accepted by keyboard.
Enter accepts a completion even when the popup is closed, breaking normal newline+indent typing.
The popup stays open after Enter, so every subsequent Enter re-accepts the same completion.

rubric.label: zustand store contract preserved
rubric.ruleStatement: The CodeMirror EditorView stays wired to the existing zustand store contract — saveCode persists each doc change into problems[currentSlug][lang] and setCursorPos tracks line/col — because this phase ships inside the editor swap and must not break the app's state wiring.
passCriteria: Every editor change fires the update listener and calls saveCode with the full document text for the active lang.
The store value problems[slug][lang] equals the editor buffer after each keystroke and after each completion insertion.
Moving the caret by typing, arrow keys, and clicks updates cursorLine/cursorCol in the store via setCursorPos.
Switching js↔ts restores each language's own saved buffer; accepting a completion never clobbers the other language's saved text.
failureExamples: Typing in the editor no longer updates the store, so running the code uses stale source.
Cursor position stays 1:1 or updates only on click, never on keyboard movement.
Switching languages after accepting a completion shows the wrong language's buffer or an empty one.

rubric.label: Completion is local, no LSP or worker
rubric.ruleStatement: Autocomplete runs fully in-process from @codemirror/autocomplete and @codemirror/lang-javascript — no language server, web worker, network request, or per-keystroke round trip — per the phase's expectedResult.
passCriteria: Completions appear in the same frame as the triggering keystroke, with no loading/pending state.
No Worker, fetch, WebSocket, or LSP-client module appears anywhere in the editor's autocomplete code path.
Autocomplete still works with the network disabled / offline.
failureExamples: The editor spins up a web worker or calls a language server endpoint to compute completions.
Completions lag or never appear because they depend on an async external source.
package.json gained an LSP client dependency to make autocomplete work.

phases.healerHint: The popup never triggers or Enter just inserts a newline because autocompletion()/completionKeymap or the matching javascript()/typescript() source isn't actually composed into the EditorView's extension array — add it there and re-test the popup-open and popup-closed Enter paths in both js and ts.

phases.name: Integrate CodeMirror theme with editor layout CSS
phases.goal: Add a CodeMirror EditorView.theme matching the existing editor metrics (var(--mono), 13px, line-height 1.62, 14px padding, tab-size 2) and style CodeMirror's built-in gutter to replace the removed .gutter; prune the orphaned .tk-*/#hl/.gutter rules from globals.css; drop CodeEditor's redundant third .editor-pane wrapper so the editor fills .editor-body without the triple-nested editor-pane.
phases.expectedResult: The CodeMirror editor visually matches the old editor (font, size, line-height, padding, working line-number gutter), fills .editor-body, obsolete .tk-*/.gutter/#hl CSS is removed, and the editor fits inside EditorPane with no CSS clash.
phases.compensation: Restore the shared stylesheet via `git checkout -- src/styles/globals.css` (CSS is shared with EditorPane) and `git checkout -- src/components/CodeEditor.tsx` for the wrapper change.

rubric.label: Theme metrics match the old editor
rubric.ruleStatement: CodeMirror EditorView.theme reproduces the old editor's metrics so the swap is visually indistinguishable: font-family var(--mono), font-size 13px, line-height 1.62, padding '14px 16px', tab-size 2.
passCriteria: CodeEditor.tsx contains an EditorView.theme() call whose fontSize is '13px' and lineHeight is '1.62'
The theme sets fontFamily to var(--mono) and tabSize: 2
The theme applies 14px top/bottom and 16px left/right padding to .cm-content, matching the old '.code-area pre, .code-area textarea { padding: 14px 16px }'
Computed style of .cm-content in the running app reads 13px / 1.62 / tab-size 2
failureExamples: Theme sets font-size 14px or omits line-height, so lines wrap or space differently from the old overlay
tabSize is omitted and pressing Tab inserts 8-space stops, breaking the 2-space indentation the old editor used
Content padding is 0, so the first token touches the gutter

rubric.label: Built-in gutter replaces the old .gutter
rubric.ruleStatement: CodeMirror's built-in line-number gutter must be styled to replicate the removed .gutter: right border, right-aligned #3d4a5a numbers at 13px/1.62 mono, and an amber current-line cue.
passCriteria: Theme includes a '.cm-gutters' rule with background var(--panel2) and border-right 1px solid var(--line-soft)
Line numbers are visible, right-aligned, and vertically aligned with the code lines (13px mono, line-height 1.62, ~14px top/bottom padding on .cm-lineNumbers)
The active line's gutter number is highlighted amber, mirroring the old '.gutter .nums div.cur { color: var(--amber) }'
Scrolling reveals numbers in a fixed-width column; the code area does not shift horizontally
failureExamples: Gutter renders unstyled (white background, no border) and is visibly distinct from the old gutter
Line numbers misalign with code lines because gutter line-height differs from the content's 1.62
No active-line highlight, so the current-line cue the old editor provided is lost

rubric.label: Orphaned overlay CSS removed
rubric.ruleStatement: globals.css must no longer contain rules that only styled the removed textarea/<pre> overlay and the hand-rolled gutter.
passCriteria: grep of src/styles/globals.css finds no .tk-kw, .tk-str, .tk-num, .tk-com, .tk-lit, .tk-fn, or .tk-cls selectors
No #hl selector remains
No .gutter or .code-area selector remains
The --mono custom property is still defined (it is shared, not orphaned)
failureExamples: '.tk-kw{color:#ffab24}' still present in globals.css — dead rules for a removed highlight engine
'.code-area textarea' block survives, matching nothing and misleading future edits
A selector survives as a partial match because the prune removed only part of a block

rubric.label: Prune didn't damage shared EditorPane CSS
rubric.ruleStatement: Because globals.css is shared with EditorPane, the prune must be surgical: only the orphaned overlay rules (.tk-*, #hl, .gutter, .code-area) are gone; every rule EditorPane still needs (.editor-pane flex sizing, .editor-head, .editor-foot, .pane-tabs, .seg, .ghost-btn, .btn-run/.btn-submit) is untouched.
passCriteria: 'git diff src/styles/globals.css' removes only selectors in the four orphaned groups — zero deletions under .editor-pane, .editor-head, .editor-foot, .pane-tabs, .seg, or .ghost-btn
In the running app EditorPane still shows its header (JS/TS toggle), footer (Run/Submit), and tabs styled identically to before the phase
Shared rules the editor still relies on (.editor-body, --mono) were not deleted
failureExamples: Prune accidentally deleted '.editor-body{flex:1;display:flex;...}', collapsing the editor region to min-height
Deleted '.editor-pane{flex:1;...}' from the shared block, breaking the whole right-hand EditorPane layout
The diff shows deletions outside the four orphaned selector groups, indicating a careless block removal

rubric.label: Editor fills .editor-body without CSS clash
rubric.ruleStatement: CodeEditor's redundant third .editor-pane wrapper is dropped and the EditorView mounts directly inside .editor-body, filling it with no nested pane, no double border, and no duplicated scrollbars.
passCriteria: CodeEditor.tsx's returned root has no className='editor-pane' (no third nested pane inside EditorPane's .editor-pane)
Live DOM for the editor region is exactly one .editor-pane > .editor-body > .cm-editor, with no .editor-pane nested inside .editor-pane

phases.name: Verification gate: build, lint, and acceptance checklist
phases.goal: Run `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build) and `npm run lint` against the swapped editor under strict + noUnusedLocals + react-hooks rules, and walk the acceptance checklist: autocomplete in js and ts; bracket/quote auto-close with caret between; no duplicated closing char; correct caret/selection after typing, bracket close, and selection replacement; setCursorPos line/column correctness; saveCode persistence; lang-switch doc load with no update loop; no Monaco code path; no web workers.
inputs: success criteria checklist from task analysis
phases.expectedResult: `npm run build` and `npm run lint` both pass on the final CodeEditor.tsx and every acceptance criterion is checked and green.

rubric.label: Build and lint gates pass
rubric.ruleStatement: `npm run build` (tsc -b && vite build) and `npm run lint` both exit 0 against the final CodeEditor.tsx under tsconfig strict + noUnusedLocals + noUnusedParameters and the eslint flat config's react-hooks rules.
passCriteria: Running `npm run build` exits 0; tsc -b reports no type errors and vite build emits a dist bundle.
No unused imports, variables, or helper functions remain in CodeEditor.tsx (noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters clean after removing the textarea/<pre> overlay code).
Running `npm run lint` exits 0 with zero errors and zero warnings against the eslint flat config.
No react-hooks/rules-of-hooks or react-hooks/exhaustive-deps violations, e.g. the EditorView mount effect lists every dependency it closes over.
failureExamples: `npm run build` fails with `'useState' is declared but its value is never read` or an unused-helper error from the removed overlay.
`npm run lint` reports `React Hook useEffect has a missing dependency: 'editorView'` or `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` on the leftover highlight function.

A type error in the EditorView.update/dispatch wiring blocks tsc -b.

rubric.label: JS/TS autocomplete present and working
rubric.ruleStatement: Directly from acceptance criterion 1 — 'Editor provides autocomplete for the language being edited (JS and TS)' — the completion popup appears in both js and ts buffers and offers language-appropriate completions supplied by @codemirror/lang-javascript, not a hand-rolled keyword list.
passCriteria: In a JS buffer, typing `cons` opens the popup listing matching keywords/identifiers (e.g. `const`, `console`); selecting one inserts it.
In a TS buffer, typing `inter` opens the popup with TS-aware completions (e.g. `interface`).
Accepting a completion inserts the chosen item and leaves the caret immediately after the inserted text.
The editor composes javascript()/typescript() with autocompletion() from @codemirror/autocomplete; no custom completion-source array exists in the component.
failureExamples: No popup appears when typing `cons` in a js buffer.
Popup appears in js mode but is empty in ts mode.
Completions come from a hardcoded string array inside CodeEditor.tsx rather than @codemirror/lang-javascript.
The popup renders off-screen or is clipped by the editor container's styling.

rubric.label: Auto-close with caret between; no duplication
rubric.ruleStatement: Directly from acceptance criterion 2 — typing `{` `(` `[` or `"` auto-inserts the closing partner and leaves the cursor between them, and typing the closing char over it does not duplicate — with closeBrackets active in both js and ts modes.
passCriteria: Typing `(` produces `()` with the caret at offset 1; typing `{`, `[`, `"`, and `'` each insert their closing partner with the caret between the pair.
With the caret between a just-inserted pair, typing the closing char advances over it — the document grows by exactly one character, never producing `())`, `]]`, or `""` duplicates.
closeBrackets is present in the EditorView extensions for both the javascript and typescript configurations.
The behavior is identical in js and ts buffers.
failureExamples: Typing `(` yields `()` but the caret lands after the `)`.
Typing `)` while the caret sits between `()` produces `())` (duplicated closing char).
Quotes fail to auto-close while parens and brackets do.
Auto-close works in js mode but not ts mode.

rubric.label: Cursor/selection correctness after edits
rubric.ruleStatement: Directly from acceptance criterion 3 — the cursor stays correctly placed after typing, bracket auto-close, and selection replacement — and extends to setCursorPos: the store-driven caret restore lands on the expected line/column and survives lang switching without misplacement.
passCriteria: Plain typing advances the caret exactly one position per character with no jumps, resets, or drift.
Bracket auto-close leaves the caret between the pair, and typing the closer moves the caret after the pair.
Replacing a multi-character selection leaves a collapsed caret at the end of the inserted replacement text.
setCursorPos(line, column) places the caret at that line/column (verified via the editor's position/coordinate query), in both js and ts docs.
After switching lang, the caret restores to the stored position of the newly loaded doc, not to the previous language's offset.
failureExamples: The caret snaps to the start of the buffer after a few keystrokes.
After replacing a selection, the caret sits before the inserted replacement text.
setCursorPos(3, 10) lands on a different line/column because the offset is computed from stale state.
Switching lang misplaces the caret because the old language's offset is applied to the new doc.

rubric.label: Zustand store contract intact
rubric.ruleStatement: The store contract — lang, state[lang] value, saveCode, and setCursorPos — stays wired through the swapped editor: edits persist via saveCode, cursor movement reports via setCursorPos, lang drives extension selection and initial content, and switching lang loads state[lang] with no update loop.
passCriteria: Typing dispatches saveCode with the new text; the store's state[lang] reflects every edit.
The editor initializes from state[lang] for the current lang and re-initializes when lang changes.
Cursor movement fires setCursorPos with the correct line and column.
Switching lang loads state[lang] exactly once and the editor never writes back during load — no update loop and no infinite re-render.
The component never mutates state[lang] directly; all writes go through the store's saveCode action.
failureExamples: state[lang] never updates as the user types because saveCode is not connected to the EditorView update listener.
Switching lang triggers a set→editor-reconfigure→saveCode cycle that loops (update loop / infinite re-render).
Cursor moves never call setCursorPos, so position persistence across sessions is lost.
The component writes state[lang] directly instead of invoking the store's saveCode action.

rubric.label: Editor stack suitable for the client-side Vite app
rubric.ruleStatement: Directly from acceptance criterion 4 — the chosen editor package must be suitable for this project: client-side only, no backend, Vite-compatible, no web workers required, reasonable bundle size — the final component and its dependency graph contain no Monaco code path, no web workers, and only @codemirror/* packages at a size befitting an editor feature, not a full IDE.
passCriteria: CodeEditor.tsx and its imports reference only @codemirror/* packages (editor-state, view, autocomplete, lang-javascript, closebrackets, theme); zero `monaco-editor` references exist.
No `new Worker(`, `Worker(` constructor, or worker plugin appears anywhere in the editor module graph.
No Node-only or backend imports (fs, path, node:*) exist in the editor's dependency graph — the app remains fully client-side and Vite-buildable.
The built editor chunk contains only @codemirror packages with no monaco-sized payload or duplicate editor engines (no codemirror 5 leftovers shipping alongside CM6).
Removing the old textarea/<pre> regex-highlight overlay also removes its dependencies from the bundle.
failureExamples: A `monaco-editor` import remains in the code path, reachable or dead.
The editor instantiates a web worker at runtime (e.g. a language-service worker).
The bundle contains node-only modules that break `vite build` for the client.
Bundle analysis shows two editor engines shipping, such as codemirror 5 remnants plus CodeMirror 6.
